newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour pro-European denies party in EMU switch.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour pro-European denies party in EMU switch.

text.p: A leading pro-European in the opposition Labour Party said on Tuesday he did not believe the party leadership was moving towards rejecting the idea of Britain joining a single currency "in the first wave".

Giles Radice, chairman of the European Movement, was asked about remarks last month by the party's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook, who said it would be hard for Britain to join a single currency immediately upon launch in 1999.
Asked whether he believed this signalled a policy shift, Radice told a news conference: "I do not. My own view is the position is exactly as it was before."

Radice said Labour leader Tony Blair had made it clear he saw "considerable advantages" in a single currency, but wanted to see whether Britain qualified to join and what the economic circumstances were at the time a decision had to be made.
"That seems to me a legitimate way for the leader of the opposition to respond," Radice said.

The news conference was held to launch a booklet which the movement is sending to 8,000 banks, financial institutions and industry bodies putting the positive case for Britain to join a single currency.
Conservative MP Quentin Davies, a vice-chairman of the movement, warned at the news conference that Britain would suffer if it was not a first-time member of a single currency.
"It is important to recognise that if we are not part of monetary union from the beginning this is not a cost-free option," he said.
Davies said British interest rates would have to be higher than those in the Euro-zone and industries would be deterred by this from investing in Britain.
